points.point: Total nonfarm payroll employment rose by 225,000 in January 2020.
points.quote: Total nonfarm payroll employment rose by 225,000 in January
paraphrases: Nonfarm payrolls added 225,000 jobs in January.
The U.S. economy added 225k nonfarm jobs last month.
January NFP print: +225,000, well above consensus.
decoys: Nonfarm payrolls added 175,000 jobs in January.
Nonfarm payrolls fell by 225,000 in January.

points.point: The unemployment rate was little changed at 3.6% in January.
points.quote: the unemployment rate was little changed at 3.6 percent
paraphrases: Unemployment rate held steady at 3.6% in January.
The jobless rate was little changed at 3.6 percent.
U.S. unemployment stayed at 3.6% last month.
decoys: Unemployment rate held steady at 3.5% in January.
Unemployment rate jumped to 3.6% in January.

points.point: Average hourly earnings rose 3.1% year-over-year in January.
points.quote: Over the past 12 months, average hourly earnings have increased by 3.1 percent.
paraphrases: Average hourly earnings rose 3.1% y/y in January.
Wage growth held at 3.1 percent year-over-year.
AHE climbed 3.1% annually in January.
decoys: Average hourly earnings rose 2.1 percent year-over-year in January.
Average hourly earnings fell 3.1 percent year-over-year in January.

points.point: Average hourly earnings rose 7 cents to $28.44 in January.
points.quote: In January, average hourly earnings for all employees on private nonfarm payrolls rose by 7 cents to $28.44.
paraphrases: Average hourly earnings rose 7 cents to $28.44 in January.
Hourly wages increased 7 cents, reaching $28.44.
The average hourly wage climbed to $28.44 in January, up 7 cents.
decoys: Average hourly earnings fell 7 cents to $28.44 in January.
Average hourly earnings rose 7 cents to $28.34 in January.

points.point: Notable job gains were concentrated in construction, health care, and transportation and warehousing.
points.quote: Notable job gains occurred in construction, in health care, and in transportation and warehousing.
paraphrases: Job gains were led by construction, health care, and transportation/warehousing.
Construction, health care, and transportation and warehousing posted the biggest payroll gains.
Hiring strength was concentrated in construction, health care, and transport/warehousing.
decoys: Job losses were concentrated in construction, health care, and transportation.
Notable job gains occurred in retail, manufacturing, and mining.

points.point: Labor force participation rate was 63.4% in January.
points.quote: the labor force participation rate edged up by 0.2 percentage point to 63.4 percent
paraphrases: Labor force participation rate was 63.4% in January.
The participation rate stood at 63.4 percent.
Labor force participation reached 63.4% in January.
decoys: Labor force participation rate held at 62.4% in January.
Labor force participation rate edged down to 63.4% in January.

points.point: Labor force participation rate edged up 0.2 percentage point in January.
points.quote: the labor force participation rate edged up by 0.2 percentage point to 63.4 percent
paraphrases: Labor force participation rate edged up 0.2 percentage point in January.
The participation rate rose two-tenths of a point in January.
Labor force participation increased by 0.2pp for the month.
decoys: Labor force participation rate edged down 0.2 percentage point in January.
The employment-population ratio edged up 0.2 percentage point in January.

points.point: November payroll gains were revised up by 5,000 to +261,000.
points.quote: The change in total nonfarm payroll employment for November was revised up by 5,000 from +256,000 to +261,000, and the change for December was revised up by 2,000 from +145,000 to +147,000.
paraphrases: November payrolls were revised up to +261,000.
The November jobs gain was revised higher by 5,000, to 261k.
November nonfarm payroll growth was revised up from 256,000 to 261,000.
decoys: November payrolls were revised down to +251,000.
December payrolls were revised up to +261,000.

points.point: December payroll gains were revised up by 2,000 to +147,000.
points.quote: The change in total nonfarm payroll employment for November was revised up by 5,000 from +256,000 to +261,000, and the change for December was revised up by 2,000 from +145,000 to +147,000.
paraphrases: December payrolls were revised up to +147,000.
The December jobs gain was revised higher by 2,000, to 147k.
December nonfarm payroll growth was revised up from 145,000 to 147,000.
decoys: December payrolls were revised down to +137,000.
November payrolls were revised up to +147,000.

points.point: Manufacturing employment changed little in January, down 12,000.
points.quote: Manufacturing employment changed little in January (-12,000) and has shown little movement, on net, over the past 12 months.
paraphrases: Manufacturing employment was little changed in January, down 12,000.
Factory payrolls slipped 12k in January, little net movement over the year.
Manufacturing jobs edged down by 12,000 in January.
decoys: Manufacturing employment rose 12,000 in January.
Manufacturing employment fell 44,000 in January.

points.point: Annual benchmark revision cut the March 2019 payroll level by 514,000, or -0.3%.
points.quote: The total nonfarm employment level for March 2019 was revised downward by 514,000 (-505,000 on a not seasonally adjusted basis), or -0.3 percent.
paraphrases: The annual benchmark revision cut March 2019 payrolls by 514,000, or -0.3%.
Benchmark revisions lowered the March 2019 employment level by 514k (-0.3 percent).
March 2019 nonfarm employment was revised down 0.3% (-514,000) in the annual benchmark.
decoys: The annual benchmark revision raised March 2019 payrolls by 514,000.
The annual benchmark revision cut March 2018 payrolls by 514,000.
